written: 2026-10-17, by hand from established, citable practice, before any run
scoring: Each dimension checklist is scored against that dimension's research document (research/<DIM>.md). The statement is the criterion; accept_any lists phrasings that count as stating it when used about the same thing. Items name practices, not pinned versions, so they stay true as libraries release.

stack.statement: Recommends a currently supported Go release (Go supports each major release until two newer ones ship) rather than an old or unsupported toolchain.
Recommends an embedded search engine rather than a server: SQLite with the FTS5 extension, or a pure-Go full-text library such as Bleve or Bluge, and explains the choice between them.
stack.basis: SQLite FTS5 documentation; Bleve and Bluge project documentation

stack.statement: If SQLite is chosen, names a driver and addresses cgo: a pure-Go driver (modernc.org/sqlite, or ncruces/go-sqlite3 via WebAssembly) for cgo-free builds, or mattn/go-sqlite3 with the cgo cross-compilation trade-off explained.
Uses github.com/fsnotify/fsnotify for file-system change notifications.
Parses Markdown with a CommonMark-compliant parser such as goldmark (github.com/yuin/goldmark) to extract text, rather than stripping syntax with regular expressions.
Parses YAML front matter with a YAML library or a goldmark front-matter extension (for example goldmark-meta, go.abhg.dev/goldmark/frontmatter, gopkg.in/yaml.v3 or goccy/go-yaml).
stack.basis: goldmark extension list; YAML library documentation

stack.statement: Chooses how to build the subcommand CLI (for example spf13/cobra, urfave/cli, kong, or the standard flag package) and says why.
Handles ignore patterns with a gitignore-compatible or glob matcher (for example a go-gitignore package, go-git's gitignore support or bmatcuk/doublestar) rather than hand-rolled matching.
Ships one static binary per platform by cross-compiling with GOOS/GOARCH, typically released with GoReleaser.
stack.basis: Go cross-compilation (go help environment); GoReleaser documentation

stack.statement: Says what not to use: no external search server (Elasticsearch, OpenSearch, Meilisearch, Typesense) for a local, single-user tool.
stack.basis: Project constraint (no server or network service) applied to the search-engine choice

features.statement: Builds a full index of the notes folder on first use by walking it recursively for Markdown files.
Updates the index incrementally: only changed files are re-indexed (detected by modification time, size or content hash), including changes made while the tool was not running.
Offers a watch mode that keeps the index current while it runs, covering created, modified, renamed and deleted notes.
Removes or moves index entries on delete and rename so searches never return stale or missing notes.
Ranks results by relevance (BM25 or an equivalent scoring function).
features.basis: SQLite FTS5 bm25() auxiliary function; Bleve scoring

features.statement: Shows a snippet for each result with the matched terms highlighted.
features.basis: SQLite FTS5 snippet() and highlight() auxiliary functions; Bleve highlighting

features.statement: Supports a query syntax with phrase queries, boolean operators and prefix matching.
features.basis: SQLite FTS5 full-text query syntax; Bleve query string syntax

features.statement: Extracts front-matter metadata, at least tags (and a title), and lets queries filter by tag.
Supports ignore patterns so configured paths are skipped (for example .git, hidden folders, attachments, or a .gitignore-style file).
Offers machine-readable output (for example a --json flag) for scripts and editor integration.
features.basis: Common CLI practice for composable tools

features.statement: Separates table-stakes features from differentiators and names what is out of scope (for example editing notes, sync or a server mode).
features.basis: Feature categorization the research workflow asks for

architecture.statement: Separates a watcher that produces change events from the indexer that consumes them, joined by a queue or channel.
Debounces or coalesces bursts of events per path before re-indexing.
architecture.basis: fsnotify README guidance on duplicate events

architecture.statement: Has a parser stage that turns each Markdown file into plain text plus metadata (title, tags, headings) before indexing.
Uses a single writer for the index (one goroutine or connection owns writes) while searches read concurrently.
architecture.basis: SQLite allows one writer at a time (sqlite.org/lockingv3.html, WAL documentation)

architecture.statement: Models storage as a search index beside the document data: with SQLite an FTS5 virtual table next to a regular notes table (external-content or contentless FTS5) keyed by note path or id; with a library, an index mapping per field.
architecture.basis: SQLite FTS5 documentation, external content tables

architecture.statement: Batches index writes in transactions (many documents per transaction or batch) for throughput.
architecture.basis: SQLite transaction cost (sqlite.org/faq.html, why INSERT is slow); Bleve Batch API

architecture.statement: Lets searches read while the indexer writes: SQLite in WAL journal mode, or the library's equivalent.
Stores per-file state (path plus modification time, size or hash) and reconciles it with a scan at startup, because events are not delivered while the tool is not running.
architecture.basis: Watchers deliver no events for changes made while stopped

architecture.statement: Keeps the index outside the watched notes tree (for example under os.UserCacheDir or an XDG data directory), or excludes its location, so writing the index does not trigger watch events.
architecture.basis: Go os.UserCacheDir; XDG Base Directory specification

architecture.statement: Lays out the code with the CLI entry point under cmd/ and the index, watch and parse logic in internal packages.
Versions the index schema (for example SQLite user_version) so an upgrade that changes the schema or tokenizer triggers a rebuild.

pitfalls.statement: fsnotify does not watch recursively: every subdirectory must be added, and directories created later must be added (and scanned) when they appear.
pitfalls.basis: fsnotify README (recursive watches are not supported)

pitfalls.statement: Editors often save atomically (write a temporary file, then rename it over the original, or remove and recreate), so the watcher must handle Rename, Remove and Create events, not only Write.
A single save or a bulk change (such as a git checkout) produces bursts of events, so indexing without debouncing repeats work.
pitfalls.basis: fsnotify README (multiple Write events per save)

pitfalls.statement: Tokenizer choice matters for non-English text: use FTS5 unicode61 with remove_diacritics (or trigram for substring and CJK search) or the library's language analyzers; the defaults handle accents and other scripts poorly.
A cgo SQLite driver breaks simple cross-compilation and CGO_ENABLED=0 static builds; choose a pure-Go driver or set up C cross toolchains.
Large trees hit watch and descriptor limits: Linux inotify max_user_watches and max_user_instances, and on macOS a kqueue backend opens a file descriptor per watched file, so ulimit matters.
SQLite returns "database is locked" (SQLITE_BUSY) under concurrent writers; use one writer, WAL and a busy_timeout.
pitfalls.basis: SQLite result codes and PRAGMA busy_timeout

pitfalls.statement: Changes made while the tool is not running produce no events, so the index drifts unless it reconciles with a scan at startup.
pitfalls.basis: Watchers only report changes while watching

pitfalls.statement: Files inside the watched tree that are not notes (the index itself, editor swap and backup files, .git) cause noise or feedback loops and must be excluded.
Passing raw user input as an FTS5 query fails on special characters (quotes, hyphens, colons, operators); queries must be escaped or quoted.
pitfalls.basis: SQLite FTS5 documentation, full-text query syntax

pitfalls.statement: Paths differ across platforms: case-insensitive file systems on macOS and Windows, Unicode normalization of file names (NFD on macOS) and path separators need normalizing before paths are used as keys.
pitfalls.basis: Apple file system Unicode normalization; Go path/filepath documentation
